corpus_definition: to damage or ruin something, or to become bad

forms.definition: the process of food going bad
forms.example: Keep milk cold to stop spoilage.

forms.definition: things taken by the winners of a war or fight
forms.example: The soldiers shared the spoils of war.
forms.note: Belongs to an old sense of spoil = take by force, not ruin.

forms.definition: to make something less good or enjoyable, or to go bad
forms.example: The bad weather spoiled our holiday.
forms.note: British English past form: spoilt or spoiled.

syn.note: Informal British English: food becomes bad.

forms.definition: gone bad, or (of a child) given too much and badly behaved
forms.example: Throw away the spoiled fruit.

ant.note: Recently made or picked, not bad.

people.definition: information that tells you what happens in a film before you see it
people.example: Don't tell me the ending, no spoilers!
people.note: Also a part on a car that helps it hold the road.

context.text: Rain spoiled our picnic in the park. Even the cake was spoiled because it got wet.

reviewer_note: spoils (war prize) is a historical sense, so other_meaning.

corpus_definition: a dirty mark on a surface that is hard to remove

forms.definition: a dirty mark that is hard to clean
forms.example: There is a coffee stain on my shirt.

syn.note: General word for a small dirty area.

forms.definition: to leave a dirty mark that is hard to remove
forms.example: Tea can stain your teeth.

forms.definition: having dirty marks on it
forms.example: He wore an old stained jacket.

forms.definition: (of steel) that does not get marks or rust
forms.example: We have stainless steel pots.

context.text: Malika spilled tea on the white tablecloth. Now there is a big stain, and the cloth is stained in two places.

corpus_definition: A small paper sticker put on a cover to pay for service.

forms.definition: a small piece of paper you stick on a letter to pay for sending it
forms.example: I need two stamps for these letters.

forms.definition: to put an official mark on a document with ink
forms.example: The officer stamped my passport.
forms.note: Also 'stamp your foot' = put it down hard, a different meaning.

syn.note: Related: put a sign on something.

forms.definition: with a stamp on it
forms.example: Send a stamped envelope with your form.

context.text: Grandpa collects stamps from many countries. He keeps every stamped envelope his friends send him.

reviewer_note: CORPUS: definition says 'cover'; normally 'envelope'. post and postage are not family.

corpus_definition: to take something that does not belong to you.

forms.definition: the crime of taking something that is not yours
forms.example: Car theft is a big problem in some cities.

syn.note: Stealing, often with force or threats.

forms.definition: the act of taking things that are not yours
forms.example: Stealing from shops is a crime.

forms.definition: to take something that is not yours without asking
forms.example: Someone stole my bike last night.

syn.note: You rob a person or bank; you steal a thing.

forms.definition: taken by someone who had no right to it
forms.example: The police found the stolen car.

forms.definition: quietly and secretly so no one notices
forms.example: The cat moved stealthily.
forms.note: Comes from stealth, an old sense of steal = move secretly.

people.example: The thief ran away with her bag.

context.text: Someone stole Aziz's phone at the bazaar. The police are looking for the thief and the stolen phone.

reviewer_note: theft and thief are family by meaning, different spelling. robber belongs to rob.

corpus_definition: a very strong, hard metal used in building and tools

forms.definition: a very strong metal made from iron
forms.example: These knives are made of steel.

syn.note: Related: the metal steel is made from.

forms.definition: to prepare yourself to deal with something bad
forms.example: She steeled herself for the bad news.
forms.note: Belongs to steel = become strong in mind, not the metal. Used as 'steel yourself'.

forms.definition: like steel in colour, or hard and strong
forms.example: He gave me a steely look.

context.text: The new bridge in our city is made of steel. The old worker looked at it with a steely, proud face.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows (B2, A2) merged; A2 used.

corpus_definition: To move a spoon in circles to mix food.

forms.definition: the act of mixing something with a spoon
forms.example: Give the soup a stir.
forms.note: 'cause a stir' = make people excited, a different meaning.

forms.definition: to move a spoon round and round to mix food or drink
forms.example: Stir the tea before you drink it.

syn.note: Mix completely, often with a machine.

forms.definition: making people feel strong emotions
forms.example: He gave a stirring speech.
forms.note: Belongs to stir = move feelings, not mixing food.

people.definition: a small stick for mixing a drink
people.example: Take a stirrer for your coffee.

context.text: Mum stirs the soup slowly with a big spoon. Give it one more stir, she tells me.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows (B1, A2) merged; A2 used.

corpus_definition: Very bad weather with heavy rain and strong wind.

forms.definition: very bad weather with strong wind and heavy rain
forms.example: A big storm hit the city last night.

syn.note: A storm with thunder and lightning.

forms.definition: to go somewhere quickly and angrily, or attack a place
forms.example: He stormed out of the room.
forms.note: Belongs to storm = move angrily, not weather.

forms.definition: with strong wind and heavy rain
forms.example: It was a dark, stormy night.

syn.note: Used about the sea in bad weather.

context.text: The weather was stormy all weekend. During the storm, two trees fell down in our street.

reviewer_note: Verb storm (move angrily) is a different meaning.

corpus_definition: A person that you do not know.

forms.definition: a person you do not know
forms.example: A stranger asked me the way to the station.

ant.note: A person you know and like.

forms.definition: the quality of being unusual or unfamiliar
forms.example: I felt the strangeness of the new city.

forms.definition: unusual, or not known to you before
forms.example: I woke up in a strange room.

forms.definition: in an unusual way
forms.example: He was strangely quiet today.

context.text: A stranger sat next to me on the bus. He was strangely quiet at first, but then we talked.

reviewer_note: Headword is a person noun, so it sits in people; strange is the base adjective. 'stranger' as comparative of strange is a separate meaning.

corpus_definition: A long thin piece of material used to tie things.

forms.definition: thin cord used for tying things
forms.example: Tie the parcel with some string.
forms.note: Also the strings on a guitar or violin.

syn.note: Very thin string used for sewing.

forms.definition: to put things on a thin cord or hang them in a line
forms.example: We strung lights across the garden.

syn.note: Put something up so it hangs.

forms.definition: (of food) long and thin and hard to chew
forms.example: This meat is very stringy.

context.text: Grandma tied the bag of apples with string. The meat in her soup was stringy, so she cooked it longer.

reviewer_note: strung is the past form of verb string.

corpus_definition: a long, thin band of colour on a surface

forms.definition: a long thin line of colour
forms.example: A zebra has black and white stripes.

syn.note: General word; a stripe is a wide line of colour.
A long narrow piece of material; easily confused.

forms.definition: having long thin lines of colour on it
forms.example: He wore a striped shirt.

context.text: Dilnoza bought a striped dress at the market. It has thin blue stripes on a white background.

reviewer_note: stripy kept as synonym of striped (same family, informal).
